example.romaji: kyou asagohan tabete nai n da.
example.ja: 今日朝ご飯食べてないんだ。

examplePolite.romaji: kyou wa asagohan o tabete inai n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 今日は朝ご飯を食べていないんです。

notes: Asameshi is a rougher version, mostly used by men.

example.english: What do you want for lunch?

examplePolite.romaji: hirugohan wa nani ni shimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 昼ご飯は何にしますか？
examplePolite.english: What will you have for lunch?

notes: Ohiru and ranchi are also common.

examplePolite.romaji: kyou no bangohan wa nan desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 今日の晩ご飯は何ですか？

notes: Yorugohan is also common, especially among younger speakers.

examplePolite.ja: お昼、一緒に食べませんか？
examplePolite.english: Would you like to have lunch together?

use: Goes before the time: gogo sanji (3 p.m.).

example.english: Sounds like it'll rain from the afternoon.

examplePolite.ja: 午後から雨らしいです。
examplePolite.english: I hear it will rain from the afternoon.

use: Mostly with clock times and schedules: gozen juuji (10 a.m.); the everyday 'morning' is asa.

example.romaji: gozenchuu wa uchi ni iru yo.

examplePolite.english: I'll be at home in the morning.

notes: Gozenchuu means 'during the morning, before noon'.

use: Roughly 4 to 7 p.m., while it gets dark; after that it's yoru.

example.english: I think I'll get there around early evening.

examplePolite.ja: 夕方ごろ着くと思います。
examplePolite.english: I expect to arrive in the early evening.

example.romaji: hiruma wa atsui kedo yoru wa suzushii.
example.ja: 昼間は暑いけど夜は涼しい。
example.english: It's hot in the day but cool at night.

examplePolite.romaji: hiruma wa atsui desu ga, yoru wa suzushii desu.
examplePolite.ja: 昼間は暑いですが、夜は涼しいです。
examplePolite.english: It's hot during the day, but cool at night.

notes: Hiru alone usually means noon or lunch; hiruma is the whole daylight stretch.

use: Mostly in set words: konban (this evening), maiban, bangohan, asa kara ban made.

example.ja: 朝から晩まで働いてる。
example.english: I work from morning till night.

examplePolite.romaji: asa kara ban made hataraite imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 朝から晩まで働いています。
examplePolite.english: I work from morning until night.

example.english: I woke up in the middle of the night.

examplePolite.ja: 夜中に目が覚めました。
examplePolite.english: I woke up in the middle of the night.

notes: Mayonaka is the dead of night.

use: Sounds more official than yonaka; used for late shifts, late-night TV and opening hours.

example.ja: 深夜までバイトしてる。
example.english: I work my part-time job until late at night.

examplePolite.romaji: shin'ya made arubaito o shite imasu.
examplePolite.ja: 深夜までアルバイトをしています。
examplePolite.english: I work part-time until late at night.

use: Same as bangohan; common at home.

example.english: I need to get dinner ready.

use: Heard at hotels, restaurants and in announcements; at home say bangohan or yuuhan.

example.romaji: yuushoku wa hoteru de taberu yo.
example.ja: 夕食はホテルで食べるよ。
example.english: We'll have dinner at the hotel.

examplePolite.ja: 夕食はホテルで食べます。
examplePolite.english: We'll have dinner at the hotel.

use: Heard at hotels and on menus; at home say asagohan.

examplePolite.romaji: choushoku wa nanji kara desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 朝食は何時からですか？
examplePolite.english: What time is breakfast served from?

notes: Lunch in the same style is chuushoku.
